rules: Completion is established only from registered record files and benchmark result.json files; never from process names, pgrep predicates, log text or a dead PID.

One atomic owner lease (O_CREAT|O_EXCL). Liveness of the recorded owner/child = PID alive AND the same process birth time. Duplicate live ownership is refused; stale ownership is refused until an explicit, recorded recover-stale.
AC power is read from 'pmset -g ps' (first line contains 'AC Power'); an unreadable or unknown power source blocks. AC is rechecked after every wait and immediately before every heavy launch.
Existing terminal benchmark results are validated and skipped without invoking benchmark.py. An occupied result directory without a valid terminal result is a BLOCKER, never an implicit rerun.
Every record, log and completion file is write-once; old logs are never opened for writing.
Terminal completion (every spec reached a terminal state) is distinct from a scientifically valid benchmark (every spec PASS with valid timing evidence and no flag).
No automatic retry of any stage. A failed or refused stage is recorded; independent later stages still run and report truthfully. No COMPLETE marker after a partial stage.
Heavy stages run strictly one at a time; no other heavy work during benchmark timings (coordination is by this lease, not by process matching).

amendment_1.kind: operational clarification only; no scientific protocol, gate, tolerance, budget, split or held-out rule changes
rules: One strict queue-completion validator serves resume, benchmark-owner release and the A2 dependency. It checks the exact expected run-name set from the registered plan, the plan hash, registration id and sha256, queue and spec identities, every spec-record hash and every underlying manifest/result/progress/log hash. A completion whose evidence was deleted or altered is invalid.

A cached command-stage record is honoured only if its registration id/sha256, source identity (tracked tree and built modules) and command equal the current ones, its waited-exit evidence is present and its log, output, retained-file and report/hashes.json evidence still hash as recorded. A foreign or stale focused-test PASS cannot authorize the diagnostic.

Spec records have a state and a completion_eligible flag. Only the terminal benchmark verdicts (PASS, FAIL, INCOMPLETE, INVALID_POWER) with complete manifest/result/progress evidence are completion-eligible; FAIL, INCOMPLETE and INVALID_POWER are terminal with flags, never PASS. A run that leaves no output (REFUSED) or a partial/malformed directory (ERROR_PARTIAL) gets a terminal execution record that blocks queue completion; it is never retried and its directory is never overwritten.

Before each spawn the lease is set to STARTING_CHILD with a handshake path. The child is a stdlib launcher that writes its PID and birth time to the handshake file and waits for an explicit go from the driver before exec of the registered command (same PID). The driver records the child identity, rechecks AC and source identity, then sends go; otherwise it sends abort and records the waited exit. An exception or signal between STARTING_CHILD and a waited exit keeps the lease (AMBIGUOUS_CHILD) and fails closed; it is never released because the child identity is absent. A successful wait() is exit evidence even when the birth time was unreadable.

Stale recovery holds an exclusive flock on a recovery lock file, re-reads the lease and revalidates its file identity (device, inode, sha256) immediately before removal. A live (including stopped) owner or child is not stale. An ambiguous STARTING_CHILD/AMBIGUOUS_CHILD lease is recoverable only if its handshake process is provably dead or reused, or with an explicit recorded operator attestation. No lease is completion proof.
benchmark.script_sha256 is enforced before any benchmark work of a queue and again with source identity and AC immediately before each launch.
A session whose record writing or lease release fails exits nonzero; no success is reported without its records.
